Triage: lands in `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` + its unit test; routed `pm:queue` + `domain:devx`, type Task. Direction: the card's disposition **3 (both)** — derive the headroom check from the report the gate just read (so drift in either direction is caught live), and re-baseline the ceiling downward as a visible, PR-stated decision. Note this is a gate **tightening** (lowering a ceiling toward reality), not a gate weakening, so it is not the manual floor — but the PR body must state the old/new constants and cite this card so the re-baseline is the recorded decision the script's header asks for. The demonstrated +153.7 KB green regression is the acceptance test: after the fix, the same injection must red. Aging note: filed 2026-08-24T01:18Z, missed by the hourly windows — swept in the daily reconciliation.

## Serialised behind PR #6210 — next in this lane, staying `pm:queue`

By the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Not a block on the merits — a file collision with a live PR, and it clears on its own.

PR #6210 (card #5490) is armed and awaiting merge, and it has `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` and `scripts/__tests__/check-eager-closure-budget.test.ts` open — the two files this card is about. Dispatching now would put two agents in both.

### What #6210 changes about this card's premise, in both directions

**It does not fix this card, and its author said so rather than widening scope.** From the PR body:

> the per-chunk headroom assertion compares two frozen constants, the same shape #5924 records for the aggregate one. The per-chunk band is ~2% rather than ~24%, so the exposure is much smaller, but the systemic fix (deriving the headroom check from the report the gate just read) belongs to that card.

So after #6210 lands this card's population **grows**: the same asserted-between-two-constants shape now exists in four places, not one — the aggregate ceiling plus three per-chunk ceilings. Re-derive it at claim time rather than carrying the card's original single-site framing.

⚠️ And a figure this card will need is now measured and different from what the neighbouring card assumed. On `2c8474c04` the closure measures **3,298,620 B** against the **4,005,911 B** baseline frozen in the file — **707 KB below it**, almost all of that shrinkage in `vendor-objectstack` (1,493 KB in the #5490 card, **926.2 KB** measured). ⭐ That makes the aggregate ceiling's live headroom **~769 KB, about 8.4× the 89 KiB regression the gate was sized to catch** — materially wider than the +153.7 KB this card's title records, and the gap widens further every time the payload shrinks without the baseline moving. #6210 deliberately left the aggregate ceiling and its baseline untouched, because #5468 ruled that line "stays as shipped" and moving it is the maintainer's call.

⛔ That last point is a boundary for this card too: **deriving the headroom *check* from the report is this card's work; moving the aggregate *ceiling* is not.** They are easy to conflate — the fix makes the ceiling's width visible, which is exactly when someone reaches to narrow it. Recording the width is in scope; changing it needs #5468's ruling revisited.

**Unblocks when:** #6210 merges. Expected within the hour — it is armed with every check green.

## ⛔ Correction to my own note above, then PM claim + dispatch order — R29

By the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Branch: `claude/issue-5924-live-headroom-invariant`.

### First: my 02:01Z note contradicted a triage ruling I had not read

I wrote:

> ⛔ deriving the headroom **check** from the report is this card's work; moving the aggregate **ceiling** is not … that needs #5468's ruling revisited.

Triage had already ruled the opposite at **00:27Z**, ninety minutes earlier — **disposition 3 (both)**: derive the headroom check live **and** re-baseline the ceiling downward as a visible, PR-stated decision, with the explicit note that lowering a ceiling *toward* reality is a **tightening**, not a weakening, so it is not the manual floor.

⛔ Triage's ruling governs; mine is withdrawn. And the substance favours it: the script's own header says re-baselining is a decision that has to be taken deliberately — **this card is that decision being taken**, recorded in a PR body where a reader can find it. #5468's "the aggregate line stays as shipped" bound the **#5490** card, which was forbidden from touching a ceiling it was not chartered to move; it was never a permanent freeze.

⚠️ How I got it wrong is the part worth recording, because it is my own standing rule: **I posted a boundary claim on this card having read its title from a list and the neighbouring PR's body — and not its comments.** "The body is the oldest thing on a card" is a line I have written into five dispatch orders tonight. Here the *comments* were the thing I skipped, on a card I was about to constrain. Third dispatch-order defect of the night from this seat.

### The order

**Scope: disposition 3, both halves.**

**(a) Derive the headroom check from the live measurement.** Today `scripts/__tests__/check-eager-closure-budget.test.ts` asserts `MAX_EAGER_CLOSURE_GZIP_BYTES - BASELINE.gzipBytes < REGRESSION_THIS_GATE_MUST_CATCH_BYTES` — both operands frozen literals in the same module, so it is true regardless of what the console weighs, and would stay true if the closure halved again. The invariant is *stated* about the live bundle and *checked* about two constants. Make the check read the report the gate just read, so drift in either direction reds the moment it opens.

⭐ **Re-derive the population at claim time — it grew since this card was written.** PR #6210 merged tonight (`48e53814e`) and added three per-chunk ceilings with `PER_CHUNK_BASELINE`, carrying **the same asserted-between-two-frozen-constants shape**. Its author flagged it and routed the systemic fix here by name. So the population is now **four** sites — the aggregate plus three per-chunk — not the single site this card's body describes. ⛔ Do not carry the card's original framing.

**(b) Re-baseline the aggregate ceiling downward, as a stated decision.** The PR body must give the old and new constants, cite this card, and say what the new headroom is as a multiple of `REGRESSION_THIS_GATE_MUST_CATCH_BYTES`. That is the record the script's header asks for.

⛔ **Do not lower any ceiling below what you measure.** #6210 landed that rule in the constant's own comment: a ceiling under today's reality lands red on `main`, which is how a budget gets switched off rather than met. Ratchet, not aspiration. Same applies to the three per-chunk lines if you touch them — and if you touch them, `PER_CHUNK_BASELINE` moves with them.

⚠️ Measure it yourself; every figure on this card is stale. The card says 3,308,221 B; #6210's dev measured **3,298,620 B** at `2c8474c04` with `vendor-objectstack` at **926.2 KB** against the card's 1,493 KB. Three consecutive builds gave byte-identical totals there, so a stable reading is achievable — take one.

### The acceptance test, from triage, and it is not optional

> the demonstrated +153.7 KB green regression is the acceptance test: after the fix, the same injection must red.

Reproduce the card's own injection — an eager `@objectstack/spec/cloud` namespace import into `apps/console/src/main.tsx`, a use the bundler cannot fold away — rebuild, and run the gate. **Predicted: exit 0 before your change (reproducing the defect), non-zero after.** ⛔ A fix you cannot first make fail is a fix you cannot show works. Then remove the injection and show the measurement returns to its exact pre-injection value, as the card did — that is what distinguishes the injection from build noise.

Prove the mutation and the restore on disk by anchored counts, never by an editor's exit code. Restore with `git checkout HEAD` followed by the explicit path, under `trap` on EXIT/INT/TERM, and prove it with an empty `git diff HEAD`.

### Bounds

⛔ Chunking is not yours: do not touch `advancedChunks` in `apps/console/vite.config.ts`. ⛔ Do not attempt a cleave — #5324 names those candidates and they are separate work. ⛔ Do not edit `content/docs/releases/`.

⚠️ `performance-budget.yml` maps exit 2 to `budget_status=error` and any other non-zero to `fail`; #6210 made `error` outrank `fail` across both halves. Whatever you change about exit codes, keep that ordering and say in the PR body that you checked it.

### Verification

Derive which tests read the files you touch and run them — `scripts/__tests__` entire, from the repo root (never package-scoped, #3378), because several files there read `apps/console/vite.config.ts` as their subject. Capture exit codes by redirect **before** any pipe. ⚠️ `node some/missing/file.mjs` exits 1, which is indistinguishable from a gate that ran and failed — a missing-file exit is a broken instrument, not a reading.

### Standing discipline

Worktree-first before your first edit. ⛔ Never `git stash` — shared stack. ⚠️ **Post a claim comment on this card carrying your session ID and branch before you write code**, in addition to anything I posted: under a shared GitHub identity mine identifies the PM session, not yours, and yours is the one a colliding agent needs (objectstack#11944 / objectstack#4588 item B).

⚠️ Lead your report with the **literal text** `os-dev-report`; write angle-bracket fragments in words; read it back after posting.

Refs: #5324 (the gauge) · #5490 / PR #6210 (the per-chunk half, merged tonight — it grew this card's population) · #5468 (the ruling that bound #5490, not this card) · #5359 (where this was found).
